deleted.title: Recover deleted files from a hard drive
deleted.metaDescription: Deleted files from a hard drive are often still there. Learn the safe steps and free tools to try to get them back before they are overwritten.
deleted.summary: When you delete a file the data usually stays until something new is written over it. The sooner you act, the better your odds. Stop using the drive now.
deleted.riskNote: You are only reading the drive, so risk is low if you follow the steps.
stopFirst: Do not save or install anything on this drive.
Do not run a disk cleaner or defragmenter.

steps.title: Stop using the drive
steps.detail: Shut the computer down or unplug the drive so nothing overwrites your files.
how: Unplug the drive and put it somewhere safe.

steps.title: Connect it to another computer
steps.detail: Use a USB adapter or dock. Do not boot from it.
how: Windows: open **File Explorer** and look for the drive in the left list. Mac: open Finder.
Type `photorec /d recovered` only if the guide tells you to, then press Enter.

steps.title: Pick a safe save location
steps.detail: You need a second drive with enough free space for recovered files.
how: Windows: open **File Explorer** and look for the drive in the left list. Mac: open Finder.
Type `photorec /d recovered` only if the guide tells you to, then press Enter.
Wait until the progress bar stops. This is safe to leave running & check later.

steps.title: Run PhotoRec
steps.detail: Choose the drive, then the save folder on the other drive. Let it finish.
how: Windows: open **File Explorer** and look for the drive in the left list. Mac: open Finder.

steps.title: Check what came back
steps.detail: Open a few files to make sure they work.
how: Windows: open **File Explorer** and look for the drive in the left list. Mac: open Finder.
Type `photorec /d recovered` only if the guide tells you to, then press Enter.

deleted.callPro: If the files are priceless or the drive starts acting strangely, stop and call a professional.

faq.q: How long do deleted files last?
faq.a: Until the space is reused. That can be minutes on a busy drive.
Yes if you save files to a different drive.

clicking.title: Hard drive clicking or beeping
clicking.metaDescription: A clicking hard drive usually has a mechanical fault. Learn what to avoid and when to go to a professional lab.
clicking.summary: Clicking often means the read heads are damaged. Running it more can make things permanently worse.
clicking.riskNote: Every power-on can scrape the platters.
stopFirst: Do not keep powering it on.
Do not put it in the freezer.

steps.title: Unplug it
